headline: High risk of shared-workspace data leakage and capability conflict; prompt-injection and cascading-error risks are moderate.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: OpenBBTerminal can use MCP and stdin/stdout, so it may ingest external content; Plandex reads/writes project files and supports review-then-apply. If OpenBB outputs untrusted text into a shared workspace, Plandex could treat it as actionable input. The pathway is plausible but not proven by docs alone.
conditions: IF OpenBBTerminal writes untrusted model output into a file that Plandex later reads
IF Plandex auto-applies changes from content originating in OpenBBTerminal
mitigations: Keep OpenBB and Plandex in separate directories
Disable auto-apply in Plandex
Manually review any OpenBB-generated files before Plandex consumes them
Use a provenance note in filenames or comments
requires-engineering: add content provenance checks between tools

B_data_leakage.rationale: OpenBBTerminal touches financial, licensed, and public data, while Plandex reads and writes project files with broad network egress. If they share a workspace, sensitive financial material can flow from OpenBB into Plandex outputs or model-provider requests. The shared filesystem path is the main risk; no stronger isolation is documented.
conditions: IF both agents operate in the same project directory or mounted workspace
IF OpenBBTerminal material is copied into Plandex prompts or files
mitigations: Use separate workspaces for each agent
Do not place financial data in Plandex project files
Redact sensitive fields before handoff
Restrict Plandex network access during sensitive tasks
requires-engineering: enforce workspace isolation at the orchestrator

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Plandex has unrestricted filesystem write, shell, subprocess, and git modification; OpenBBTerminal can use MCP and multiple instances. If both touch the same repo or directory, concurrent edits and state changes can collide, and Plandex’s shared backend plus OpenBB’s multi-instance support increase the chance of race conditions. This is dangerous by default in shared workspaces.
conditions: IF both agents can write to the same directory or git repository
IF Plandex runs with shell/git permissions while OpenBB uses the same workspace
mitigations: Assign each agent a separate repo clone
Pause one agent before the other writes
Disable git writes in Plandex for shared repos
Use file locks around shared outputs
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level mutual exclusion

D_cascading_error.rationale: Plandex is a planner that stages changes and can auto-apply, so it may act on OpenBBTerminal-produced content without independent verification. OpenBBTerminal can emit financial analysis or model output that Plandex could treat as authoritative input. The pair creates a plausible chain from generated content to applied changes, but not an irreversible default action path.
conditions: IF Plandex consumes OpenBBTerminal output as a task specification
IF auto-apply is enabled or review is skipped
mitigations: Require human review before apply
Separate analysis output from action prompts
Add a verification checklist for OpenBB-derived claims
Keep auto-apply disabled
requires-engineering: add schema validation for handoff artifacts

E_compliance.rationale: OpenBBTerminal explicitly touches financial and licensed data, while Plandex sends prompts to a model provider or cloud/server backend. If regulated financial or licensed content is placed into Plandex, retention or residency obligations may differ from OpenBB’s local workflow. The mismatch is compliance-relevant, though not enough evidence exists for a higher severity.
conditions: IF regulated financial or licensed data is entered into Plandex prompts or files
IF the model provider or Plandex Cloud retains data beyond the operator’s policy
mitigations: Avoid sending regulated data to Plandex
Strip identifiers before prompting
Review provider retention settings
Use self-hosted endpoints where possible
requires-engineering: document a data-processing agreement and retention policy
